speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To understand your condition of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after antibiotic treatment, can you tell me which specific antibiotic you were prescribed and for what infection?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-Associated Morbilliform Drug Eruption with Arthralgia.

Given the specific timing (one week after starting amoxicillin), the distribution of the rash (starting in flexural areas like antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading), and the accompanying joint pain, this presentation is highly suggestive of a delayed hypersensitivity reaction to amoxicillin. The clinical picture is consistent with a drug-induced exanthem and arthralgia. No further testing is required at this time as the diagnosis is made based on the clear temporal relationship and characteristic rash distribution. I will ensure the antibiotic is discontinued and provide supportive care instructions.
